original_card.question: Can a changed G20 helper path or independent-target split improve the complete BIT moment without losing its physical endpoint?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: First read #5679/#5708 and their audits as pending component proposals. Choose one uncovered helper group/cut on an exact word; compare arbitrary-input native action, targets, owned storage, both orientations and full signed bill. Stop if the gain is only a scalar count or repaid by lost targets. Do not rerun the frozen #5609 common-frame domain without changing its hypothesis.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: On the emitted PR5708 word and its published one-edge route table, move exactly two corrections of each A2 conjugation with exactly five contacts onto other frames, leave the other corrections on their contact frames, and decide whether any such assignment lowers the paid-query moment on (0,1).
scope_change_reason: The card says to review the #5679/#5708 chain and stop when a proposed cut does not improve the paid moment. #6664 shows that two moved corrections fail to emit at 2, 3 and 4 contacts. #6923 shows that one moved correction fails to lower the moment at length at least 5, and leaves the two-move question open. This package takes that question on the length-exactly-5 slice: every such interval, not a single sample.
bottleneck_link: A paid-moment obstruction on this exact word says the length-5 two-move conjugation domain does not raise the ordinary BIT component. It does not change the selected exponent.
stop_rule: Stop when every two-move frame pair on the 133 intervals of length exactly 5 is classified. Do not open a length-6 search or a three-move search in this package.
evidence: python3 -I -B research/g20-length5-two-move/verify.py prints PASS_G20_LENGTH5_TWO_MOVE with assignments=536289250, tail_missing=4331, emitted=0 and savings=0.

open_questions.question: Can two corrections in one interval of length at least 6 lower the paid moment when both frames move?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This census classifies every two-move pair at exactly five contacts. PR #6664 stops at four contacts and PR #6923 moves only one correction at length at least 5, so length 6 and above is the remaining two-move clause on this word and route table.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate one length-6 interval's two-move pairs on this word and one-edge route table. The length scan records 86 such intervals.
open_questions.blocked_by: No favorable witness is supplied. None of the 536,289,250 length-5 assignments emits, and a length-6 interval is a different finite domain.

open_questions.question: Can three or more moved corrections in one length-5 interval emit and lower the paid moment?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Exactly two corrections move in this census. A third moved frame can change a tail that currently misses an edge.
open_questions.first_step: On one of the 4,331 length-5 words that survive both moved meetings and then miss a later edge, move one further correction and price that word.
open_questions.blocked_by: Those 4,331 words are rejections, not saving seeds. A search that moves a third correction on some of them would be a partial search unless its domain is finite and fully enumerated.
